meta.purpose: THE REGISTER OF CONTROLLED VOCABULARIES. Every word-group / lookup used anywhere in IBA is defined here, once, and assigned a code — and nowhere else. If a field anywhere in the application accepts only a fixed set of values, that set is an item in this file and the field points at its code. A vocabulary defined in a doc, a SQL CHECK, or a module's source is a defect, not a second opinion.
meta.why_it_exists: The programme currently has the same concept defined 3-4 ways across the REF doc, the DB wa_vocab_* tables, free-text SQL columns, and synced patch copies — with divergent values. Enforcing one home with one code is the fix (plan C.13 item 6, recon.vocab-home).
meta.envelope: Every item carries the common rule envelope — see _manifest.json meta.envelope. Its vocabularies (governs · kind · status · validation.axis · validation.severity) are defined there and are NOT restated here.

nodes.items: The vocabularies themselves. One item = one word-group = one code (`id`) = one lookup. Full envelope + the `spec` below.

spec_schema.description: The kind-specific body for kind=enum. What the vocabulary actually contains.

values.description: THE OPTIONS — the permitted values of the vocabulary, and the only ones any field bound to this code may hold. On a RECONCILE item this is the WORKING set (see `canonical`), not authority.

canonical.description: Whether `values` IS the decided, authoritative set. false = contested; the item's status will be RECONCILE, `reconcile` names the open decision, and `values` is a placeholder the loader will not run study modules on.

reconcile.description: The `recon.*` id in reconciliations.json holding the open decision that settles this vocabulary.

variants.description: The divergent value-sets found across sources, keyed by source. This is the evidence for the decision — kept so the reconciliation is made against what the sources actually say, not from memory.

alias_map.description: Maps superseded/variant values onto the canonical one, so historic data stays readable after the decision. Feeds the loader's import mapping.

default.description: The value assumed when the read finds nothing to the contrary (e.g. device defaults to `literal`). A default is NOT the same as `none`: default = the unmarked normal case; `none` = assessed and genuinely absent.

labels.description: Human-readable expansion where the value is a code rather than a word (e.g. segment_unit_type D = discourse). ⚠ ad-hoc — see meta.open.value-metadata.

rule.description: A constraint on USE of the vocabulary that domain-membership alone does not capture (e.g. resolution: `none` and `unknown` are distinct and must never be conflated).

note.description: Anything a reader needs to interpret the item — typically why the stored data diverges from the rule.

legacy_pre_reset.blocked_by: meta.open.legacy-scope — decide whether the new config carries LEGACY vocabularies at all

open.issue: A value is a bare string. There is no per-value home for its meaning, its ordinal, or its aliases — so enum.segment_unit_type invented a side-map (`labels`), enum.role's aliases sit in a separate `alias_map`, and every other vocabulary's values are simply undefined. The plan's cfg_enum table expects value + ordinal + notes (A.3), which this shape cannot supply.
open.consequence: Values cannot be self-interpretable — the same defect the read layer failed on (dimrule.self-interpretable). A reader of `enum.locus` cannot tell what `external:world` includes without going back to the source doc, which is exactly the drift this register is meant to end.
options: A: keep bare strings; accept that value meanings live in the source docs (cheapest; does not meet cfg_enum; values stay uninterpretable)
B: values become objects { value, description, ordinal?, aliases? } — self-interpretable, matches cfg_enum, absorbs `labels`/`alias_map`; costs a rewrite of the 11 authored items before expansion
C: hybrid — bare strings allowed where the value IS its own definition (e.g. `action`/`status`/`quality`), objects required where it is not
open.recommendation: B, decided BEFORE expansion — the register is 11 of ~50+ items; changing the value shape after authoring the rest is the expensive order. Applying your own self-interpretable rule to the config is also the consistent one.

open.issue: The plan's new DB carries no legacy (3.4.2 'no legacy/quarantine carry-over'), but the envelope defines a LEGACY status and the README says superseded rules are marked, not deleted. It is not decided whether pre-reset vocabularies (session_b_status, cluster.*, the pre-reset flag sets) belong in this register as LEGACY or are simply out of scope.
open.consequence: Roughly a dozen vocabularies are either in scope or not; it materially changes the size of this file.
options: A: author them as LEGACY — the old DB stays readable and the archive stays interpretable
B: out of scope — the new config describes only the new model; the old DB's vocabularies stay documented in the old DB and the archive
open.recommendation: B for anything the new DB never stores, A for anything that arrives with the migrated registry/term layer (those values will be present in new-DB rows, so the new config must define them).

open.issue: For most outstanding vocabularies the authoritative member list is in the live DB (wa_vocab_set/wa_vocab_member) or a SQL CHECK, not in a doc.
open.consequence: Authoring them from the docs or from memory would re-import the very drift this register exists to end.
open.resolve_by: Pull members from the live DB once, as a one-time seed extraction, and author from that — per recon.vocab-home's recommendation. Needs a read-only extract script before expansion.

definitional_ruling.statement: An enum defines the ITEM, its OPTIONS, and WHERE IT IS USED (governs). How it is APPLIED is process configuration.
definitional_ruling.applied: 2026-07-15 — stripped every `validation` block, `spec.default` and `spec.rule` from this register.

where_they_went.the domain check: a gate in the process that uses the vocabulary (e.g. gate.lexical.value-in-domain, gate.char.role-domain), citing the enum by id

definitional_ruling.consequence: A definitional item has no `validation` of its own — see ../_manifest.json meta.open.definitional-kinds. `validation` is therefore optional in the envelope for definitional kinds.

self_hosting.authority: researcher ruling 2026-07-15 (a) — no nomenclature without its description in the enums
self_hosting.statement: This register holds the configurator's OWN vocabularies too. They are nomenclature like any other and get no exemption for being meta.
self_hosting.bootstrap: The kernel loads this register first with envelope checks only, then validates everything — including this register — against it. It knows the envelope; it never knows a vocabulary VALUE.

items.satisfaction: every `kind` field value is one of spec.values

values.description: A controlled vocabulary — a word-group/lookup defined once, assigned a code, listing its permitted options.
A ve_nr lexical dimension: its shape, pair-direction, mandatoriness, derivability.
A genre × role mandatory-dimension set — which dimensions are required for a given genre and role.
A validation gate or measure: integrity invariants, content-validity, drift, coverage, acceptance-sample.
A functional pipeline module: its order, handler, enable flag, scope.
An edge in the module dependency graph: what a module needs first, and whether a missing prerequisite auto-activates or halts.
Standing methodological guidance (the nine principles, infer-don't-extract, convergence-validity). Governs how reads are done; mostly [I].
A naming/filing/label/patch/versioning pattern.
An operational parameter: model tier, DB path, thresholds, retries, budget caps, debug level.
A provenance or completion convention: markers, STATED-vs-INFERRED, completeness-as-validity, soft-delete discipline, field-authority.
A behavioural constraint drawn from the failure record that the app enforces (no-forced-structure, plausibility≠truth, resist-grouping, completeness≠validity).

A contested-value decision: one concept defined divergently across sources, needing ONE canonical value + an alias map. Carries its own decision-status vocabulary, not vocab.status — see wide/reconciliations.json meta.

A data entity a process owns — what it IS, its grain, its identity, what it holds, and which layer it belongs to. ADDED 2026-07-15 (the process files need it). ⚠ BOUNDARY: an entity item does NOT declare tables, columns or types — that is the schema's job (layout v2 §1). It says what the data MEANS; the schema says what structure holds it.
A human-facing artefact a process emits — projections, review packs, reports. Never authoritative: the DB is the source and every output is regenerable (plan §3.6). ADDED 2026-07-15.
A conditional routing rule — which treatment applies under which condition (genre routing being the live case). ADDED 2026-07-15; anticipated by plan A.3 cfg_route.

A rule governing an IBA utility rather than a study process. ADDED 2026-07-15 per the researcher's ruling that each utility gets its own json. Utility files are not yet authored — see meta.open.utility-set.

spec.nature_note: `nature` marks each kind DEFINITIONAL (it defines what a thing IS — enum, dimension, entity, output, reconciliation) or ENFORCEMENT (it constrains or wires — gate, module, dependency, route, pattern, setting, utility) or STANDING (principle, provenance, guardrail). Per the researcher's 2026-07-15 ruling, a definitional item defines the item, its options, and where it is used; HOW IT IS APPLIED is a separate enforcement rule with its own home. This is why `validation` is not-applicable on definitional kinds — see meta.open.definitional-kinds.
spec.open: `kind` is NO LONGER 1:1 with a file (layout v2 §2.2) — it selects the SPEC-SCHEMA; the file selects the process or utility. The `section` field is retired for the same reason. Still undefined: a kind for governance (GR-*/FLAG-*/interaction protocols). See meta.open.missing-kinds.

items.subject: status
items.authority: researcher ruling 2026-07-15 (a) — no nomenclature without its description in the enums
items.intent: The lifecycle state of a rule. Applies to every item EXCEPT reconciliation items, which use their own decision-status vocabulary.
items.satisfaction: every `status` field value is one of spec.values

values.description: The current, authoritative rule. This is what the application enforces.
A superseded rule, kept for provenance and marked, never deleted — so old data and old reads remain interpretable. The application does not enforce it and must not write new data under it.

The concept is real but its VALUE is contested — the same rule is defined divergently across sources and the canonical form is not yet decided. A researcher decision, tracked in reconciliations.json. THE LOADER REFUSES TO RUN ANY STUDY MODULE THAT DEPENDS ON A RECONCILE RULE until it is resolved: a contested rule is a known-unknown, and running on one is how the study banked invalid data before. A RECONCILE item's `spec` may carry a working value plus its `variants`; the working value is NOT authority.

items.subject: axis
items.authority: researcher ruling 2026-07-15 (a) — no nomenclature without its description in the enums
items.intent: How a rule is validated — the [C]/[I] boundary. Nearly every rule is [C]; only Screen 0, role assignment, and the semantic content of sense/operation/reading plus pair-bindings are genuinely [I] (plan §4).
items.satisfaction: every `axis` field value is one of spec.values

values.description: Deterministic — checkable in code with no model involved (domain membership, shape, pair-direction, not-null, arithmetic, parity). Runs over the whole corpus in seconds, gives the same verdict every time, and CANNOT be overridden by the model. This is where the application's reliability comes from.

Interpretive — requires genuine inference, so the model produces it and a [C] gate then checks the output and retries on violation. The model never self-certifies: an [I] value that fails its [C] gate does not bank. Used only where the meaning genuinely cannot be derived mechanically.

⚠ PRESENT IN dimensions.json (`spec.derivation`) BUT NOT A VALID `validation.axis` VALUE. Means: morphology narrows the candidates but the choice still needs inference. Currently only ever appears as a derivation, never as an axis — see meta.open.axis-vs-derivation.

spec.note: `validation.axis` takes C or I only. `spec.derivation` on a dimension is a DIFFERENT field with an overlapping vocabulary (C · I · I-partial · read-only) — the two are not the same thing and must not be conflated. See meta.open.axis-vs-derivation.

values.description: A CHECK constraint projects this rule (typically a domain drawn from an `enum.*` item).
A foreign key projects this rule (a referential invariant).
A NOT NULL constraint projects this rule (a mandatory-value rule).
An index projects this rule (a uniqueness or access requirement). Uniqueness invariants live here.
The validation engine enforces it. Everything a DB constraint cannot express: multi-table, conditional, arithmetic, distributional, or interpretive-output checks.
Both — the DB rejects the plainly-invalid, and a gate carries the part the constraint cannot express. Defence in depth for a red control.

spec.note: A rule whose enforcement is `db:*` still lives HERE in full. The constraint is downstream. See iba/docs/iba-configurator-layout-v2-20260715.md §1.1.
